chunkSize.title: "Chunk" here is a download file-transfer block size (for future resume support), not a job's keyspace chunk.

table.slow: Column header; flags a slow (computationally expensive) hash algorithm, not table performance.
table.salted: Column header; flags a hash type that uses per-hash salts, which affects keyspace calculation.

tooltips.processing: Badge label shown on a hash type that needs special code-level processing; not a 'loading' indicator.

providers.preflight: Button that runs a read-only readiness check (credentials, quota); it launches nothing itself.
providers.acknowledge: Button confirming the admin accepts the third-party data-exposure risk described nearby.

fields.vpnTag: Label for the VPN tag/group (e.g. a Tailscale ACL tag) assigned to rented instances, not a generic tag field.
fields.awsUseSpot: "Spot" refers to AWS EC2 Spot (discounted, interruptible) capacity, not a location.

providers.limitsValue: Template for a provider's limits; {{instances}} is the max concurrent instance count and {{rate}} is the hourly cost cap.

zones.colZone: Column header for an AWS Availability Zone, not a time zone or generic area.
zones.availableCount: "{{count}} free" means {{count}} machines currently available to rent, not 'free of charge'.

trust.measured: Displayed text is 'live', meaning this figure was just fetched in real time from the provider (vs. a static/advisory number).

actions.drain: Status meaning no new work is dispatched to this client while its in-flight chunks finish, just before a hard stop.

columns.client: "Client" is the customer/engagement being billed, not a software client.
columns.ttl: "TTL" (time to live) is the maximum lifetime allowed for a rented instance before forced teardown.

fields.enabled: "Cloud burst" is the feature name for letting this client's jobs rent paid cloud GPU capacity; this is the toggle, not a status.

fleet.destroy: Row action that terminates (deletes) a rented cloud instance and stops its billing, not a data-deletion action.
fleet.teardownFailingTitle: "Teardown" is the process of destroying/releasing a rented cloud instance.
fleet.estimated: Abbreviation for 'estimated'; the figure is projected from elapsed time and rate, not the provider's final billed amount.

states.draining: Instance lifecycle state: no new work is sent while its current in-flight chunk finishes before teardown.

columns.rate: Column header for the instance's hourly billing rate, not a hash rate or success rate.
columns.spend: Column header (noun use of 'spend') showing the dollar amount this instance has cost so far.
columns.client: "Client" is the customer/engagement this instance's work is billed to, not a software client.
columns.agent: "Agent" is the cracking-machine process running on this rented instance, not a person.

fields.minStarvation: "Starvation" is scheduling jargon for a job getting no agent time at all; sets the minimum wait before that triggers cloud rental.

system.reconciliation: Heading for the background process that checks the database against what the cloud provider is actually running, not financial reconciliation.

units.seconds: Unit abbreviation 's' for seconds, used as a numeric-field suffix.

fields.teardownSlack: "Slack" means a time buffer reserved before an instance's lifetime ends, not the Slack messaging app.
fields.commissioningGrace: "Commissioning" is the startup period after a rented instance registers, before it has done any work.
fields.reaperInterval: "Reaper" is the background process that destroys stray/unrecognized cloud instances; sets how often it runs.
fields.orphanGrace: "Orphan" means an instance found on the cloud provider's account with no matching database record.
fields.crackDrainGrace: Combines 'crack' (cracked password) and 'drain': how long to wait for a dying instance to finish uploading cracked passwords before destruction.

system.discard: Button that discards unsaved form changes on this settings page, not a destructive data action.
system.eligibility: Heading for a toggle deciding whether jobs may be offloaded to rented cloud capacity at all, separate from spend limits.

summary.subject: "Subject" is the X.509 certificate field naming who the certificate was issued to, not a topic.
summary.serial: "Serial" is the certificate's unique serial number, not a product serial number.

discovered.hits: Column: how many times this address has been seen attempting to connect; not a security 'attack hit' count.

rotateCa.instruction: {{phrase}} is a literal confirmation word/phrase the admin must type to proceed.

banner.body: {{agents}} is either 'An agent' or a count/name list (paired with title_one/title_other), used as the sentence's subject.

sections.execution: Short nav label for 'Job Execution' settings (chunking, keyspace, benchmarks), not a general sense of 'execution'.

cards.binaries: Dashboard card for managed hashcat binary files, not numeric/binary data.

attention.migration: {{state}} holds a storage-migration phase/status string (e.g. 'in progress', 'failed').

fieldState.applyHint: "Apply" refers to a specific Apply button elsewhere on the page; this field only takes effect once that button is clicked.

branding.replace: Button to replace the already-uploaded logo or favicon image with a new one.

agentAutoUpdate.healthTimeout: "Health" refers to whether an updated agent reconnects successfully, not general system health.

agent.exportPath: "Export path" is NFS terminology for the directory path exposed by the network share, not a data-export feature.

attackModes.straight: Hashcat's name for a plain dictionary (wordlist) attack, not 'straightforward'.
attackModes.association: Hashcat attack mode that maps each hash to one specific candidate password by line number, not a generic grouping.

filters.apply: Button that applies the selected filters to the analytics view.

successRate.preset: Badge marking a row as a built-in preset job configuration, as opposed to a custom one.

columns.totalCompute: "Compute" means total GPU time spent (a compute resource), not a count of computations.

jobExecution.taskBreakdown: {{tasksPhrase}} and {{metricsPhrase}} are pre-built phrases like '5 tasks' and '120 metric points'.

columns.benchmark: Column showing the agent's measured hash rate for this job, not a general performance score.

columns.clients: "Clients" means customers/engagements assigned to this team, not software clients.
columns.agents: "Agents" means cracking machines accessible to this team's members, not people.

tabs.trustedTeams: "Trusted" teams are other teams whose agents may run this team's jobs — a specific one-way permission, not general trust.

detail.addTrust: Button to grant another team's agents permission to run this team's jobs, not a generic 'add trust' action.
detail.systemOwner: Value shown in place of a username when an agent is owned by the system itself rather than a team member.

columns.source: Column showing whether an agent is 'Direct' (owned by a team member) or 'Trusted' (borrowed from a trusted team).

source.direct: Means the agent is owned by a member of this team, as opposed to borrowed from a trusted team.

roles.admin: This is the team-level 'Admin' role, distinct from the system-wide Admin user role.

typeLabels.hex: "Hex" marks a charset defined as hex byte pairs rather than literal characters.
